question.text: What do red, yellow and green signal lights at intersections control?

answer.text: Red, yellow and green signal lights stand at many intersections to control the direction and flow of traffic.

teaching.text: At many intersections, red, yellow and green lights direct traffic and control how it flows. Remember: direction and flow.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Red, yellow and green signal lights stand at many intersections to control the direction and flow of traffic.

question.text: Besides motorists, who must obey traffic lights?

answer.text: Traffic lights bind pedestrians and bicycle and moped riders as well as motorists.

teaching.text: Pedestrians and bicycle and moped riders must follow traffic lights just as drivers do. Remember: walkers and riders too.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Traffic lights bind pedestrians and bicycle and moped riders as well as motorists.

question.text: When may you do something other than what the signal light shows?

answer.text: You must obey the signal lights unless a police officer directing traffic tells you to do otherwise.

teaching.text: Follow the signal lights unless a police officer directing traffic tells you to do something else. Remember: when an officer directs.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: You must obey the signal lights unless a police officer directing traffic tells you to do otherwise.

question.text: Which wins, an officer's directions or the signal light?

answer.text: A police officer's directions override what the signal light shows.

teaching.text: When a police officer is directing traffic, the officer's directions win over the signal light. Remember: the officer.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A police officer's directions override what the signal light shows.

question.text: What does a green light allow?

answer.text: A green light means you may go through the intersection in the direction the signal allows, if the roadway is clear.

teaching.text: A green light lets you go through the intersection in the allowed direction, as long as the roadway is clear. Remember: go if clear.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A green light means you may go through the intersection in the direction the signal allows, if the roadway is clear.

question.text: What should you do before entering an intersection on green?

answer.text: Even on green, look left and right for cross traffic before entering, so a red-light runner does not hit you.

teaching.text: Before you roll into the intersection on green, look left and right so a driver running the red does not hit you. Remember: look left and right.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Even on green, look left and right for cross traffic before entering, so a red-light runner does not hit you.

question.text: On a fresh green, whom must you yield to?

answer.text: On a fresh green, yield to any vehicle that was already in the intersection when the light changed.

teaching.text: When your light has just turned green, let any vehicle still in the intersection finish crossing first. Remember: vehicles already inside.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: On a fresh green, yield to any vehicle that was already in the intersection when the light changed.

question.text: What does a steady yellow light warn you of?

answer.text: A steady yellow light warns that the signal is about to turn red.

teaching.text: A steady yellow light is a warning that red is about to come on. Remember: red is coming.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A steady yellow light warns that the signal is about to turn red.

question.text: What should you do on a steady yellow light?

answer.text: On a steady yellow, stop safely if you have not yet entered the intersection, but if you are already in it, keep going and clear it safely.

teaching.text: If you have not entered yet, stop safely on a steady yellow; if you are already in the intersection, keep going and clear it. Remember: stop if not yet inside.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: On a steady yellow, stop safely if you have not yet entered the intersection, but if you are already in it, keep going and clear it safely.

question.text: May you speed up to beat a yellow light?

answer.text: Speeding up to beat a yellow light is illegal and could cause a crash.

teaching.text: Speeding up to get through on a yellow light is against the law and could lead to a crash. Remember: never race the yellow.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Speeding up to beat a yellow light is illegal and could cause a crash.

question.text: What must you do at a red light?

answer.text: On a red light, come to a complete stop before the intersection, stop line or crosswalk, and stay stopped as long as the light is red.

teaching.text: At a red light, stop completely before the intersection, stop line or crosswalk and remain stopped while it stays red. Remember: stop and stay stopped.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: On a red light, come to a complete stop before the intersection, stop line or crosswalk, and stay stopped as long as the light is red.

question.text: How does a steady yellow differ from a steady red?

answer.text: A steady yellow tells you the red is coming, so you stop if you can do so safely before entering, whereas a steady red requires a complete stop and waiting for as long as it stays red.

teaching.text: A steady yellow means stop if you can do it safely before entering, while a steady red means a full stop and a wait for as long as it lasts. Remember: yellow warns, red holds.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A steady yellow tells you the red is coming, so you stop if you can do so safely before entering, whereas a steady red requires a complete stop and waiting for as long as it stays red.

question.text: When may you turn right on a red light?

answer.text: Unless a sign forbids it, you may turn right on red after a complete stop once vehicles and pedestrians are clear.

teaching.text: After a complete stop, you may turn right on red once vehicles and pedestrians are clear, unless a sign forbids it. Remember: full stop, then right.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Unless a sign forbids it, you may turn right on red after a complete stop once vehicles and pedestrians are clear.

question.text: What two conditions apply to a right turn on red?

answer.text: A right turn on a steady red needs a complete stop first and is barred wherever a sign prohibits it.

teaching.text: Turning right on red takes a complete stop first, and a sign can forbid it altogether. Remember: stop first, check signs.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A right turn on a steady red needs a complete stop first and is barred wherever a sign prohibits it.

question.text: What does the manual's freeway-exit figure show about slowing down?

answer.text: The manual's freeway-exit figure shows the correct exit: do not slow down on the freeway itself, slow down in the exit lane.

teaching.text: The manual's figure shows the right way to exit a freeway: keep your speed on the freeway and slow down in the exit lane. Remember: slow in the exit lane.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: The manual's freeway-exit figure shows the correct exit: do not slow down on the freeway itself, slow down in the exit lane.

question.text: What does a flashing red light mean?

answer.text: A flashing red light means the same as a stop sign: stop fully, then go on with caution when the way is clear.

teaching.text: Treat a flashing red light like a stop sign: stop completely, then continue carefully when the way is clear. Remember: flashing red, full stop.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A flashing red light means the same as a stop sign: stop fully, then go on with caution when the way is clear.

question.text: What does a flashing yellow light mean?

answer.text: A flashing yellow light means slow down and proceed with caution if the roadway is clear.

teaching.text: A flashing yellow light tells you to slow down and continue with caution if the roadway is clear. Remember: flashing yellow, slow down.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A flashing yellow light means slow down and proceed with caution if the roadway is clear.

question.text: How does a flashing red light differ from a flashing yellow light?

answer.text: A flashing red light is treated as a stop sign, while a flashing yellow light only requires slowing down and proceeding with caution.

teaching.text: Flashing red works like a stop sign, but flashing yellow only asks you to slow down and go carefully. Remember: red stops, yellow slows.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A flashing red light is treated as a stop sign, while a flashing yellow light only requires slowing down and proceeding with caution.

question.text: What does a lighted red arrow mean?

answer.text: A lighted red arrow means you may not turn in its direction; stop and wait for the green signal before turning.

teaching.text: A red arrow forbids turning in its direction, so stop and wait for the green signal. Remember: red arrow, no turn.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A lighted red arrow means you may not turn in its direction; stop and wait for the green signal before turning.

question.text: What does a yellow arrow warn of?

answer.text: A yellow arrow is the warning that the arrow signal is about to turn red.

teaching.text: A yellow arrow warns that the arrow signal is about to change to red. Remember: arrow turning red soon.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A yellow arrow is the warning that the arrow signal is about to turn red.

question.text: What should you do facing a yellow arrow?

answer.text: Facing a yellow arrow, stop and wait for a green arrow if you have not entered the intersection, or finish your turn and clear it safely if you already have.

teaching.text: On a yellow arrow, stop and wait for green if you are not yet in the intersection, or finish your turn and clear it if you are. Remember: stop, or finish if inside.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Facing a yellow arrow, stop and wait for a green arrow if you have not entered the intersection, or finish your turn and clear it safely if you already have.

question.text: Should a driver already in the intersection stop for a yellow arrow?

answer.text: A yellow arrow is a warning that red is next, and a driver already inside the intersection should finish the turn and clear it rather than stop.

teaching.text: A yellow arrow warns that red is next, and a driver already inside the intersection should finish the turn rather than stop. Remember: inside? finish the turn.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A yellow arrow is a warning that red is next, and a driver already inside the intersection should finish the turn and clear it rather than stop.

question.text: What does a flashing yellow arrow allow?

answer.text: A flashing yellow arrow lets you turn with caution after slowing, if the roadway is clear and you first yield to any oncoming vehicle or pedestrian.

teaching.text: A flashing yellow arrow lets you turn carefully after slowing, once the roadway is clear and you have yielded to oncoming vehicles and pedestrians. Remember: yield, then turn.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A flashing yellow arrow lets you turn with caution after slowing, if the roadway is clear and you first yield to any oncoming vehicle or pedestrian.

question.text: How does a red arrow differ from a flashing yellow arrow?

answer.text: A red arrow forbids the turn until a green signal appears, while a flashing yellow arrow permits the turn after you yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.

teaching.text: A red arrow forbids the turn until green, while a flashing yellow arrow allows it once you have yielded. Remember: red forbids, flashing yields.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A red arrow forbids the turn until a green signal appears, while a flashing yellow arrow permits the turn after you yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.

question.text: What does a green arrow allow?

answer.text: A green arrow, alone or with another light, lets you go in the arrow's direction if you are in the proper lane and the roadway is clear.

teaching.text: A green arrow, alone or with another light, lets you move in its direction from the proper lane when the roadway is clear. Remember: go the arrow's way.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A green arrow, alone or with another light, lets you go in the arrow's direction if you are in the proper lane and the roadway is clear.

question.text: How do you treat an intersection whose signal is not working?

answer.text: Treat an intersection whose traffic signal is not working as a four-way stop: stop completely before entering, then go when the roadway is clear.

teaching.text: If an intersection's signal is not working, treat it as a four-way stop: stop completely, then go when the roadway is clear. Remember: dark light, four-way stop.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Treat an intersection whose traffic signal is not working as a four-way stop: stop completely before entering, then go when the roadway is clear.

question.text: At a dark signal, who goes first when two vehicles arrive together?

answer.text: When two vehicles reach such an intersection at about the same time, both stop and the driver on the left yields to the driver on the right.

teaching.text: When two vehicles arrive at a dark signal together, both stop, and the driver on the left lets the driver on the right go first. Remember: left yields to right.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: When two vehicles reach such an intersection at about the same time, both stop and the driver on the left yields to the driver on the right.

question.text: At a dark signal, how is a tie between two vehicles settled?

answer.text: At a dark signal both vehicles stop, and the tie goes to the driver on the right.

teaching.text: At a dark signal, both vehicles stop, and the one on the right goes first. Remember: both stop, right goes.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: At a dark signal both vehicles stop, and the tie goes to the driver on the right.

question.text: At a T intersection, who must yield?

answer.text: At a T intersection, the driver on the street that ends must yield to vehicles on the cross street.

teaching.text: At a T intersection, the driver whose street ends must yield to traffic on the cross street. Remember: ending street yields.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: At a T intersection, the driver on the street that ends must yield to vehicles on the cross street.

question.text: At a T intersection, which driver yields?

answer.text: At a T intersection it is the driver on the street that ends who must yield to traffic on the cross street.

teaching.text: At a T intersection, the driver on the ending street is the one who yields. Remember: the ending street.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: At a T intersection it is the driver on the street that ends who must yield to traffic on the cross street.

question.text: What do you follow at a controlled intersection?

answer.text: At controlled intersections, obey the signals and signs and yield to other vehicles as they direct.

teaching.text: At a controlled intersection, follow the signals and signs and yield the way they tell you to. Remember: obey signs and signals.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: At controlled intersections, obey the signals and signs and yield to other vehicles as they direct.

question.text: Does having the right-of-way make it safe to go?

answer.text: Having the right-of-way does not by itself make it safe to go; check for traffic and pedestrians first.

teaching.text: Even when you have the right-of-way, check for traffic and pedestrians before you go. Remember: check before you go.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Having the right-of-way does not by itself make it safe to go; check for traffic and pedestrians first.

question.text: Where do you stop at a controlled intersection?

answer.text: At a controlled intersection, stop at the stop line.

teaching.text: At a controlled intersection, make your stop at the stop line. Remember: stop at the line.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: At a controlled intersection, stop at the stop line.

question.text: How is an intersection with no lights or signs treated?

answer.text: An intersection with no traffic lights, stop signs or yield signs is treated as a four-way stop, with a full stop before entering.

teaching.text: An intersection with no lights, stop signs or yield signs is treated as a four-way stop, with a full stop before you enter. Remember: no controls, four-way stop.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: An intersection with no traffic lights, stop signs or yield signs is treated as a four-way stop, with a full stop before entering.

question.text: How are a dark signal and an uncontrolled intersection handled?

answer.text: A dark traffic signal and an intersection with no signals or signs at all are handled the same way, as a four-way stop.

teaching.text: A dark signal and an intersection with no signals or signs are handled the same way, as a four-way stop. Remember: both are four-way stops.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A dark traffic signal and an intersection with no signals or signs at all are handled the same way, as a four-way stop.

question.text: Does the law ever give a driver the right-of-way?

answer.text: The law requires certain vehicles to yield to others; it never actually gives the right-of-way to any driver, it only says who must yield.

teaching.text: Right-of-way law only says who must yield; it never actually hands the right-of-way to any driver. Remember: law names who yields.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: The law requires certain vehicles to yield to others; it never actually gives the right-of-way to any driver, it only says who must yield.

question.text: When may no one take the right-of-way?

answer.text: No one may take the right-of-way if taking it could cause a crash.

teaching.text: Nobody may take the right-of-way when doing so could cause a crash. Remember: never into a crash.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: No one may take the right-of-way if taking it could cause a crash.

question.text: In which crosswalks must you yield to pedestrians?

answer.text: You must yield to pedestrians crossing the street in any crosswalk, whether it is marked or unmarked.

teaching.text: Yield to pedestrians crossing in any crosswalk, whether it is painted or not. Remember: marked or unmarked.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: You must yield to pedestrians crossing the street in any crosswalk, whether it is marked or unmarked.

question.text: After your light turns green, whom must you still yield to?

answer.text: After your light turns green you must still yield to pedestrians and vehicles that are in the intersection.

teaching.text: Once your light turns green, you still yield to pedestrians and vehicles that are in the intersection. Remember: still yield on green.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: After your light turns green you must still yield to pedestrians and vehicles that are in the intersection.

question.text: When must you stop at a school crossing?

answer.text: The law requires a complete stop at any school crossing while anyone is in the crosswalk.

teaching.text: At any school crossing, the law requires a full stop while anyone is in the crosswalk. Remember: anyone in the crosswalk.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: The law requires a complete stop at any school crossing while anyone is in the crosswalk.

question.text: May you pass a vehicle that has stopped for a pedestrian?

answer.text: You may not pass a vehicle that has stopped for a pedestrian, even if your lane is clear or your signal is green.

teaching.text: Never pass a vehicle that has stopped for a pedestrian, even if your lane is clear or your light is green. Remember: never pass a stopped car.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: You may not pass a vehicle that has stopped for a pedestrian, even if your lane is clear or your signal is green.

question.text: What two pedestrian rules apply at school crossings and stopped vehicles?

answer.text: A school crossing stop is required whenever anyone is in the crosswalk, and a vehicle stopped for a pedestrian may never be passed, even on green.

teaching.text: Stop at a school crossing whenever anyone is in the crosswalk, and never pass a vehicle stopped for a pedestrian, even on green. Remember: stop and never pass.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A school crossing stop is required whenever anyone is in the crosswalk, and a vehicle stopped for a pedestrian may never be passed, even on green.

question.text: Whom does the manual say to give the right-of-way to for safety?

answer.text: For safety, give the right-of-way to anyone you see crossing any street.

teaching.text: For safety, let anyone you see crossing any street go first. Remember: anyone crossing.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: For safety, give the right-of-way to anyone you see crossing any street.

question.text: What do flashing and solid yellow mean on a pedestrian-activated signal?

answer.text: At a pedestrian-activated crosswalk signal, flashing yellow means a pedestrian has pressed the signal, and solid yellow means prepare to stop.

teaching.text: At a pedestrian-activated signal, flashing yellow means someone pressed the button, and solid yellow means get ready to stop. Remember: pressed, then prepare.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: At a pedestrian-activated crosswalk signal, flashing yellow means a pedestrian has pressed the signal, and solid yellow means prepare to stop.

question.text: How do flashing and solid yellow differ on a pedestrian signal?

answer.text: Flashing yellow on a pedestrian-activated signal means a pedestrian has pressed the button, while solid yellow means prepare to stop.

teaching.text: On a pedestrian signal, flashing yellow means the button was pressed, and solid yellow means prepare to stop. Remember: flashing pressed, solid stop.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Flashing yellow on a pedestrian-activated signal means a pedestrian has pressed the button, while solid yellow means prepare to stop.

question.text: What do solid red lights mean at a pedestrian crosswalk signal?

answer.text: Solid red lights at a pedestrian crosswalk signal mean stop, because a pedestrian is in the crosswalk.

teaching.text: Solid red at a pedestrian crosswalk signal means stop, because someone is in the crosswalk. Remember: solid red, walker crossing.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Solid red lights at a pedestrian crosswalk signal mean stop, because a pedestrian is in the crosswalk.

question.text: What do flashing red lights mean at a pedestrian crosswalk signal?

answer.text: Flashing red lights at a pedestrian crosswalk signal mean stop, then go on with caution after the pedestrian has crossed the driver's half of the road.

teaching.text: Flashing red at a pedestrian crosswalk signal means stop, then go carefully once the pedestrian has crossed your half of the road. Remember: stop, then go when clear.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Flashing red lights at a pedestrian crosswalk signal mean stop, then go on with caution after the pedestrian has crossed the driver's half of the road.

question.text: How do solid red and flashing red differ on a pedestrian signal?

answer.text: On a pedestrian-activated signal, solid red means stop and stay stopped while the pedestrian is in the crosswalk, whereas flashing red means stop and then go once the pedestrian has cleared your half of the road.

teaching.text: Solid red on a pedestrian signal means stay stopped while someone is in the crosswalk, while flashing red means go once they clear your half. Remember: solid waits, flashing clears.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: On a pedestrian-activated signal, solid red means stop and stay stopped while the pedestrian is in the crosswalk, whereas flashing red means stop and then go once the pedestrian has cleared your half of the road.

hooks_spoken: Green means go when clear, a steady yellow means stop if you can safely, and you never speed up for a yellow.
recap.narration_text: Time for a quick review of green, yellow and red lights. Green means go when clear, a steady yellow means stop if you can safely, and you never speed up for a yellow. Keep these ideas handy as you practice.

hooks_spoken: On red, stop fully and wait; turn right only after a full stop where no sign forbids it.
recap.narration_text: Time for a quick review of stopping on red. On red, stop fully and wait; turn right only after a full stop where no sign forbids it. Keep these ideas handy as you practice.

hooks_spoken: Flashing red is a stop sign, flashing yellow means slow down, a red arrow forbids the turn and a flashing yellow arrow means yield, then turn.
recap.narration_text: Time for a quick review of flashing lights and arrows. Flashing red is a stop sign, flashing yellow means slow down, a red arrow forbids the turn and a flashing yellow arrow means yield, then turn. Keep these ideas handy as you practice.

hooks_spoken: Treat a dark signal or an uncontrolled intersection as a four-way stop, and yield to the right when you arrive together.
recap.narration_text: Time for a quick review of intersections without signals. Treat a dark signal or an uncontrolled intersection as a four-way stop, and yield to the right when you arrive together. Keep these ideas handy as you practice.

hooks_spoken: Yield to pedestrians in any crosswalk, stop at occupied school crossings, and never pass a vehicle stopped for a pedestrian.
recap.narration_text: Time for a quick review of yielding to pedestrians. Yield to pedestrians in any crosswalk, stop at occupied school crossings, and never pass a vehicle stopped for a pedestrian. Keep these ideas handy as you practice.
